version.value: Complete French setting for tenor, mixed chorus and orchestra; Suzanne Karpelès’s French text.
version.note: The source names Sénéchal for this work, rather than a tenor group. The precise performing edition is not identified. Music and translation rights are distinguished below.

performers.note: Per-work soloist headings were visually read, not inferred from a whole-album creator tag. Markevitch is the conductor; Nadia Boulanger is separately credited with recording supervision. J. J. Grunenwald is named only for the works whose scores contain organ. The ensemble credits are album-level; individual instrumental players and exact section numbers are unestablished.

date.note: No dated session log was established. The 1960 release year, 2021 transfer date and 2023 derivative-generation date are not recording dates.

place.note: The sleeve explicitly states that the recording was made at the Salle Pleyel on Everest equipment; this is not inferred from the orchestra’s home city.

label.note: Original mono LP imprint; the original copyright credit is Belock Instrument Corp.

catalogue.note: SDBR 3059 is the separately identified stereo counterpart, not the transferred catalogue number.

composition.value: Underlying work clearance is not established: Boulanger died in 1918, but the French translator Suzanne Karpelès died in 1968.
composition.note: A separate ordinary life-plus-70 calculation would put Boulanger’s music out of term, but Karpelès’s translation term would run through 2038. Directive 2011/77/EU also provides a last-survivor term when words and music were specifically created for the same composition; whether that condition applies here has not been established. No permission or applicable text exception is established. The programme’s sound-recording rule 3 is satisfied separately; phonogram expiry is not underlying-work clearance. No lyrics or their translation are reproduced in the guide.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial EU sound-recording public domain: lawful publication documented by 1960, before 1963.
recording.note: The original commercial mono release LPBR 6059 is dated 1960; the sleeve carries ©1960 Belock, corroborated by the label discography. The rule concerns first lawful publication anywhere, not first EU publication. On the former fifty-year term this phonogram was no longer protected before the 2013 extension. US recording status is not established. No worldwide public-domain claim, Creative Commons licence or modern-remaster release is inferred.

Territorial EU rule 3; US recording status not established.

sources.locator: Album header: Igor Markevitch conducting Orchestre Lamoureux and Chorale Elisabeth Brasseur; organ J. J. Grunenwald; named soloist roster; recording direction Nadia Boulanger. Psalm 130’s individual heading names Oralia Dominguez and Raymond Amade.

sources.locator: Official stereo counterpart page identifies Dominguez and Amade for Psalm 130; Sénéchal for Psalm 24 and Vieille prière; Mollet for Psalm 129; Fauqueur for Pie Jesu. This corroborates the visually inspected mono insert; the stereo stream is not used.

sources.title: Lili Boulanger — original Durand full score
sources.locator: Printed pp. 1, 8–12, 17–18, 23–24. Two harps share one icon. Sarrusophone is written but has no stage icon; no substitution is inferred. Trumpets are present in the full score despite their omission from the short nomenclature list. The French sung text has separate unresolved rights; no lyrics are reproduced here. Representative passage snapshots, placed approximately using the cached level/novelty report and score order. Not continuous player detection; individual rests are not mapped.

sources.title: IMSLP — work and publication record
sources.locator: General Information: composition and publication dates, scoring, text and work identity. The linked original full score was opened and visually inspected; this catalogue page alone is not used to infer instrumental entrances.

sources.title: Library of Congress — Lili Boulanger
sources.locator: Biographical dates 1893–1918; first woman to win the composition Prix de Rome in 1913; Villa Medici and the sisters’ wartime support work.

sources.title: Directive 2006/116/EC — term of protection
sources.locator: Articles 1 and 8: ordinary authorial life-plus-70 term and calculation from the following 1 January; Article 3’s historical phonogram term is read with the 2011 extension’s transition rule. Recording and composition rights remain separate.

sources.title: Directive 2011/77/EU — phonogram extension and transition
sources.locator: Article 1(3), inserting Article 10(5): extended phonogram protection applies to recordings still protected on 1 November 2013. The 1960 publication evidence puts this recording’s former fifty-year term before that transition. Article 1(1), inserting Article 1(7), separately gives a last-survivor term for words and music specifically created together. Its applicability to this translation is not established. Territorial EU basis only; no worldwide or US clearance.

sources.title: Everest LPBR 6059 — visually inspected per-track insert
sources.locator: Individual work heading supplies the named soloist for Vieille prière bouddhique. Notes by David Noakes; ©1960 Belock footer on the final insert leaf. For Psalm 129, the preceding continuation on the last leaf describes women’s wordless closing voices.

sources.title: Scholarly preface — Vieille prière bouddhique
sources.locator: Helen Julia Minors (2011) for the psalms; Konstantin Galluhn (2010), English translation Bradford Robinson, for Vieille prière. Composition, performance history and score structure. Speculative psychological readings and unsupported numerical symbolism are not adopted.

sources.title: BnF — Suzanne Karpelès authority record
sources.locator: International form Karpelès, Suzanne (1890–1968); death 7 November 1968 at Vellore. Distinguishes the French translator’s term from Boulanger’s musical copyright.
